newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Oct 18.

text.p: The Belgrade bourse on Monday reported a 25.9 percent decline in its weekly turnover and traders said the market reflected a lack of liquidity and was growing wary ahead of the November 3 general elections.

The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said its turnover during the week ending October 18 fell to 22.83 million dinars ($4.48 million) from 30.82 million dinars ($6.1 million), while the number of deals inched up to 165 from 162.

Most traders attributed the plunge to a lack of funds needed to bolster the market. But according to one trader, the liquidity increased towards the end of the week, with no explanation where the money came from.
However, a market analyst said investors were obviously growing cautious ahead of the elections.

"Maturity on commercial paper and treasury bills is clearly cut down and investors are trying to close positions before the elections, fearing possible post-elections dinar devaluation and its effects," the analyst, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The market became increasingly sensitive to orchestrated support to dinar stability coming mainly from government ministers and politicians ahead of November 3.
"But we have learned a lesson from the past, and it would be no surprise to see the dinar devalued shortly after the elections," another analyst said.
Some traders saw no improvement for the market once the elections are over.
"A market can only perform under stable circumstances, and we do not have such stability," a trader said.
Apart from elections, traders were a lot more worried by recent central bank signals that the current 10 percent reserve requirement would have to go up.

"The central bank has to mop up surplus liquidity. It must neutralise the effects of a recent expansion in money supply which rises faster than prices. But it really gave us the shivers. An increase in the reserve requirement would be another blow to the already illiquid market," a trader said.
With the reserve requirement up, banks would withdraw funds from the market, another trader said.
In the meantime, the BSE reported no deals in the central bank short-term bonds over the last week.
The commercial paper segment continued to dominate the bourse activity, with 138 deals worth 15.97 million dinars.
Treasury bills were traded 22 times for a volume of 3.3 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills remained unchanged and ranged between an annual 331 and 793 percent.
The bourse reported two deals in wheat selling forward contracts worth 2.8 million dinars. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
